title: API and Routing Technical Reference
readerIntent: Audit route contracts and generated API evidence.
owner: Owning route module and Nodics Router
summary: A route contract includes transport, exposure, context, security, controller, response, OpenAPI, operational, and testing metadata.

sections.heading: Ownership and request path
items: The router exposes a versioned transport contract; controllers adapt HTTP; pipelines apply shared processing; owning services authorize, validate, and execute business behavior.
A route declares method, path, operation, input source, API exposure, token classes, permissions, tenant requirements, limits, response handler, and stable status codes.
Do not place business logic in controllers or create direct provider/database calls that bypass generated models and services.

sections.heading: Security and context
items: Only human login routes accept username and password before authentication. Employee, customer, internal service, and scheduled routes retain distinct token and audience contracts.
Resolve trusted tenant and enterprise context, enforce exact route permissions, schema/field/ownership policy, body and query limits, CORS, CSRF, and safe headers.
Public errors omit secrets, stacks, paths, personal data, and policy detail while correlation supports protected diagnosis.

sections.heading: Mutation and compatibility
items: Mutations define idempotency, optimistic revision, validation, uncertain timeout behavior, compensation, and durable workflow handoff where required.
Version response fields and semantics deliberately; compatible additions, deprecation periods, consumer evidence, migration, and removal are documented.
Generated OpenAPI and clients consume the backend route authority and never become a competing contract.

sections.heading: Verification and operations
items: Test success, malformed input, missing and wrong token, denied permission, wrong tenant, field masking, ownership, duplicate mutation, conflict, timeout, and provider failure.
Verify pagination, maximum sizes, rate and body limits, direct-module communication, mono and distributed topology, load, cancellation, observability, and regression.
Measure request rate, latency, status category, saturation, timeout, and dependency outcome with bounded labels; document service objectives and runbooks.

sections.heading: Checklist
items: Versioned URL, method, operation, controller, request type, and owning module.
secured, authTokenTypes, permission or permissionConfig, and apiExposure.
Tenant/enterprise requirements, headers, query/body limits, cache policy, and idempotency.
Stable success/error codes, public response fields, trace behavior, and OpenAPI.
Positive, negative, boundary, contract, integration, security, load, and regression tests.

sections.heading: Generated routes
paragraphs: Generated CRUD routes are real contracts traced to schema and route source. Fix the source metadata or generator; never patch generated output as authority.
Regenerate, validate, contract-test, security-test, and independently review derived routes whenever authoritative schema or route metadata changes.
